a:r.a:t: The process for cloning via BAC is very similar to using plasmids.
Often, a colorimetric approach using X-gal is employed to select for colonies containing the chromosomal insert.

p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram shows the process of cloning DNA with bacterial artificial chromosomes. The top of the diagram begins with a bacterial vector, shaped like a ring and containing multiple colored regions. It is labeled BAC vector in the middle. The top of the ring has a short red section is labeled “cloning sites (within IacZ).” There is a short yellow section on either side of the red section. The long green section on the left is labeled, “F plasmid par genes.” To the right of this is a long yellow section, and to the right of this is a tan section labeled “ori.” To the upper right of this is a short yellow section, and above this is a gray section labeled “camR.” To the left of this is a short yellow section, connected left with the top red section. Below this is a down arrow with blue text on the left reading, “restriction endonuclease.” The image below shows the vector breaking at the red cloning site at the top of the ring. Below this is a down arrow with blue text reading, “DNA ligase” to the left. To the upper right of the down arrow is a long, curved blue DNA fragment with red ends, labeled “large DNA fragment with appropriate sticky ends” at the top. This has a convergent arrow below it that merges with the main down arrow. Below, the ring has broken and is in a “c” shape on the left. Its broken red ends have bonded to the red sticky ends on the large DNA fragment. The recombinant BAC (labeled right) is now a long, stretched-out loop. The blue section is to the right. In the center there is text reading, “LacZ gene (red) disrupted; no b-galactosidase produced.” Below is a down arrow labeled “electroporation” to the left. Below this is a bacillus bacterial cell, off-white in color with a blue, stringy mass of genetic material on the left end. The recombinant BAC is now inside the cell, on the right end. Below is a down arrow labeled “selection of CamR cells.” Below this arrow is a petri dish with yellow agar and 4 small white colonies and 3 small blue colonies. The agar is labeled, “Agar containing chloramphenicol and X-gal” at the upper right, and “Colonies with recombinant BACs are white” below.
